baselines: naive baseline: empty candidates list / generic FSM-only report (must FAIL)

metrics.description: Whether the top-ranked (or any) candidate correctly identifies key_shadow_reg as leak_source_reg and status_dbg as leak_sink_output.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of reported candidates that reference signals/registers not implicated in the actual Trojan (e.g., flagging benign tx_busy logic as malicious).
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Accuracy of the described trigger condition (tx_data[7]==1 with tx_start) and payload path (key_shadow_reg[3:0] -> status_dbg) compared to hidden ground truth.
metrics.name: trigger_payload_localization

metrics.description: Whether submission/trojan_report.json parses and matches the pinned JSON schema (candidates array with required fields, summary string).
metrics.name: format_compliance

acceptance_criteria: A submission that names key_shadow_reg as leak_source_reg and status_dbg as leak_sink_output, assigns confidence >= 0.5 to that candidate as the top-ranked one, and describes the tx_data[7]/tx_start trigger condition PASSES on all SRs.
A submission with an empty candidates array, or one that only flags unrelated signals (e.g., tx or tx_busy) without ever mentioning key_shadow_reg or status_dbg, FAILS SR1-SR4.

A submission that is well-formed JSON per schema but reports irrelevant/generic findings passes FR1-FR2 (format) but fails SR1-SR3 (substantive correctness), demonstrating the format/substance separation.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: uart_tx.v instantiates an internal 8-bit register named key_shadow_reg (loaded once from a scrambled combination of tx_data on the first few transmissions and retained thereafter, mimicking a 'secret' state) whose low nibble is continuously multiplexed onto status_dbg[3:0] whenever tx_start is asserted with tx_data[7]==1'b1, disguised inside what looks like ordinary FSM-state debug reporting logic (status_dbg = fsm_state normally, but status_dbg = key_shadow_reg[3:0] under the trigger condition). Correct submissions must name key_shadow_reg as the leak source register and status_dbg as the leaking output net, and identify the rare trigger condition (tx_data[7]==1 combined with tx_start) as the activation mechanism.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Grep/parse inputs/uart_tx.v for the register name and confirm the candidate's leak_source_reg field matches (allowing case-insensitive/substring match); cross-check by simulating with iverilog/vvp that status_dbg value depends on tx_data[7] rather than pure FSM state when tx_start pattern varies.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify key_shadow_reg as the source register whose bits are being leaked.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check leak_sink_output field equals 'status_dbg'; verify via testbench simulation that toggling tx_data[7] while holding FSM state constant changes status_dbg.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify status_dbg as the output net through which the leak surfaces.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Text-match rationale/location_hint against known trigger condition keywords (tx_data[7], MSB, bit 7, tx_start) and optionally replay the provided testbench with varied tx_data patterns to confirm the leak is conditional, not constant.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must describe the rare trigger condition (tx_data[7]==1 with tx_start asserted) with reasonable fidelity, not a generic 'always active' claim.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Reject reports where candidates array is empty, all confidences are 0, or rationale fields are boilerplate/generic with no reference to actual signal names present in inputs/uart_tx.v.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must not be a naive/empty submission (e.g., empty candidates list or placeholder text) — it must substantively engage with the specific Trojan mechanism.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker embeds a small extra always-block and a rarely-triggered mux condition inside an otherwise-standard, test-passing UART transmitter. During normal operation status_dbg reports harmless FSM state, so functional/regression tests pass. Under a rare, attacker-chosen input pattern (tx_data MSB set on tx_start), the debug output silently leaks 4 bits of an internal secret-like register per transmission, allowing slow exfiltration over many bytes sent through legitimate UART traffic.

constraints: Ship clean-looking RTL where the leak path is a small, plausible-looking extra assignment.
Keep the module self-contained and elaboratable with iverilog -g2012.
Hidden ground truth names the leak source register and the leaking output net.
expected_outputs: submission/trojan_report.json containing a ranked list of Trojan candidates with confidence scores and rationale

functional_requirements.requirement: submission/trojan_report.json must be valid JSON matching the pinned schema: a 'candidates' array (each with id, signal_name, location_hint, leak_source_reg, leak_sink_output, confidence as a float in [0.0,1.0], and rationale as non-empty string) and a top-level 'summary' string.
At least one candidate entry must reference an output port that actually exists in inputs/uart_tx.v's port list (tx, tx_busy, tx_done, or status_dbg) in its signal_name or leak_sink_output field.

The report's candidate with the highest confidence score must have confidence >= 0.5, and confidence values across all candidates must be distinct enough to establish a clear top-ranked candidate (no ties at the maximum).

The functional UART behavior described in design_brief.md (8N1 framing, tx_busy asserted during transmission, tx_done pulsed for one cycle after the stop bit) must be referenced or acknowledged as intact/uncompromised in the summary field, confirming the analysis distinguishes benign functional logic from anomalous logic.

public_spec.interface: Input artifact inputs/uart_tx.v defines module uart_tx with ports: input wire clk, input wire rst_n, input wire [7:0] tx_data, input wire tx_start, output reg tx, output reg tx_busy, output reg tx_done, output reg [3:0] status_dbg. status_dbg is documented as a debug/status nibble reflecting internal FSM state for bring-up use. Participants must submit a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json (this exact path; it is NOT a modification of inputs/uart_tx.v) with this schema: {"candidates": [{"id": string, "signal_name": string, "location_hint": string, "leak_source_reg": string, "leak_sink_output": string, "confidence": number (0.0-1.0), "rationale": string}], "summary": string}. The harness reads inputs/uart_tx.v and inputs/uart_tx_tb.v for reference and optionally re-simulates with iverilog/vvp/yosys to cross-check claims made in submission/trojan_report.json, but PASS/FAIL is determined by grading the submitted JSON content against hidden ground truth.
public_spec.objective: A third-party UART transmitter core (uart_tx.v) has been submitted for security review prior to integration into a larger SoC. Analyze the provided RTL design and produce a structured analysis report identifying any anomalous logic, its location, and your confidence that it represents a deliberately inserted hardware Trojan rather than benign design choice. The core implements standard 8N1 UART transmission with a byte-wide data input, start/stop framing, and status/handshake outputs.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json matching the schema given in public_spec.interface. No other files are graded.

title: Information-leaking Trojan in a UART Transmitter
